extracted.intended_audience: medical researchers, science/health journalists, press officers and science communication researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing accuracy and presence of 'spin' in press releases and related news coverage for two‑arm, parallel‑group randomized controlled trials by comparing press releases and media items to the original scientific article (especially the abstract conclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: "Spin" (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Spin," defined as specific reporting strategies (intentional or unintentional) emphasizing the beneficial effect of the experimental treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the central evaluative construct for abstracts, press releases, and news items. The paper identifies and classifies instances of spin and gives examples (see Figure 3) of the kinds of statements/strategies that constitute spin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of spin in scientific article abstract conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Spin" was identified in 28 (40%) scientific article abstract conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract conclusions should be examined for reporting strategies that overemphasize benefit; presence of spin in abstract conclusions was measured and used as a predictor variable for downstream misrepresentation in press releases and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of spin in press releases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess press releases for the same types of spin as in abstracts (overly positive framing, emphatic benefit statements despite nonsignificant primary outcomes, etc.). The study used systematic identification procedures and reports prevalence; examples are provided in the paper's figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of spin in news items / media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: News items identified for RCTs were reported with "spin" in 21 (51%) of cases, mainly the same type of "spin" as in the press release and article abstract conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating news coverage, check whether the article mirrors the press release's framing or amplifies spin from the scientific abstract; compare wording and claims to the original article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overestimation of RCT findings in press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of RCTs based on press releases were overestimated for 19 (27%) reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the press release conveys an effect size or interpretation that is more favorable than justified by the trial's reported results (e.g., presenting nonsignificant primary outcomes as beneficial). The study operationalized and counted such overestimations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overestimation of RCT findings in news items
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of RCTs based on the news item were overestimated for ten (24%) reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess news items for overstatement of trial findings relative to the scientific article; note whether the overestimation mirrors the press release or introduces additional exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to assess as potential predictors of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: The study assessed journal type, funding source, sample size, type of treatment (drug or other), results of the primary outcomes (all nonstatistically significant versus other), author of the press release, and the presence of "spin" in the press release's associated article abstract conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bivariate and multivariable analyses to evaluate which contextual or trial characteristics are associated with higher likelihood of spin; in this study the only factor independently associated with spin in press releases was spin in the article abstract conclusion (RR 5.6, 95% CI 2.8–11.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative assessment against the original article (procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain a copy of the scientific article to which the press release relates and systematically search for related news items to compare claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methodology requires direct comparison between press release / news wording and the original trial report (particularly abstract conclusions and primary outcome results). The paper searched press releases (EurekAlert!), obtained the associated scientific article, and searched Lexis Nexis for news items—this comparative approach is required to detect misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and classification of spin types
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of "spin" in abstracts, in press releases, and in related news items are provided (see Figure 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating communications, consult concrete examples of spin to classify the type of misrepresentation (e.g., focusing on within‑group comparisons, emphasizing secondary outcomes, language implying effectiveness despite nonsignificance). The paper's examples can be used as a reference/anti‑pattern checklist.
